title: Add
summary: git add stages changes: it chooses exactly what goes into the next commit.

levels.title: Stage a file
levels.briefing: Git does not save every file automatically. The staging area is a list of what will go into your next commit, and git add puts a file's current content on that list.

cheatsheet.description: See what is staged and what is not

hints: git status lists both files as untracked.
git add takes the name of the file you want to stage.
levels.successMessage: hello.txt is now staged for the next commit, and notes.txt is still untracked.

levels.title: Stage everything
levels.objective: Stage every file in this folder at once.
hints: You could add the files one by one, but there is a shortcut.
A dot means "everything in this folder".
levels.successMessage: git add . stages every change in the folder in one go.

levels.title: Stage a folder
levels.objective: Stage only the files inside the src folder.
hints: git add accepts a folder name as well as a file name.
Giving a folder stages everything inside it.
levels.successMessage: Adding a folder stages every file inside it, and nothing outside it.

levels.title: Create and stage
levels.objective: Create a file called todo.txt and stage it.
hints: The file has to exist before you can stage it.
Create it with touch or echo, then add it.
Run: touch todo.txt, then git add todo.txt
levels.successMessage: New files are untracked until you stage them with git add.
